title: Pain and pleasure: affective somatosensory processing and emotion regulation in borderline personality disorder (BPD)
summary: In our project we want to examine sensory processing in borderline personality disorder and the underlying neural mechanisms. In addition, the relationship between sensory processing and social & emotional processes as well as underlying psychopathology (symptom severity) will be examined. For this purpose, we will examine these processes in people with borderline personality disorder and non-clinical controls (for comparison). In comparison to non-clinical controls, we expect people with borderline personality disorder to have altered sensory processing and ratings of pain and pleasant touch.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
german speaking, capability to provide informed consent 

Additionally for clinical participants: bpd diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
For every participant:
- Existing substance dependence
- Existing or past bipolar disorder
- Existing or past schizophrenia
- Use of psychotropic drugs (except SSRIs & SNRIs) within seven days prior to study participation  
- Use of pain drugs three daays prior to study participation
- Exclusion in MRI study, if MRI compatibility is not given.

For healthy subjects: 
- Existing mental illness
